title: Cutler-Twining memo (MJ-12, 14 July 1954)
provenance: A one-page memorandum dated 14 July 1954 from Robert Cutler to General Nathan Twining that Jaime Shandera and William Moore reported finding in July 1985 in Record Group 341, Entry 267, at the National Archives. The Archives says it "poses problems": the series is filed by Top Secret register number and it bears none; its marking "Top Secret Restricted Information" came into use at the National Security Council only under Nixon; it has no letterhead or watermark; the NSC minutes hold no meeting on 16 July 1954; and Cutler was abroad on 14 July 1954. Stanton Friedman judged it "almost certainly genuine", answering that Cutler had left instructions with NSC executive secretary James Lay. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds a copy marked "BOGUS" by hand.
